rationale: Evidence from iteration 0 (R2A): all 60 trials ran off track on all three development tracks, so none finished. Mean max_error was 0.062 to 0.067 m, just above the 0.06 m off-track limit, and rms_error was about 0.03 m. Line-loss events averaged 1 to 2 per run. The sensors span only +/-0.03 m, narrower than the 0.06 m offset at which the robot leaves the track. Once the robot drifts that far, the outer sensors read nothing, the line is lost, and the robot runs off. Steering oscillation (about 0.14 to 0.17) and the high kp gain (4.0) with a 1.6 base speed also leave little margin for the bends. Changes: (1) widen the sensor array to x = -0.05, -0.025, 0, 0.025, 0.05 so the line stays visible at larger offsets. The weights keep the same antisymmetric pattern (-1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1), so the sign convention still steers correctly. (2) Lower base_speed from 1.6 to 1.4 so the robot can track the line before it reaches the limit. This trades some completion time for survival, which matters because a run that leaves the track scores only about 60. (3) Raise kd from 0.2 to 0.3 to damp the oscillation, and reduce ki from 0.1 to 0.05 to limit integral overshoot on bends. kp stays at 4.0. Expected result: fewer line-loss events, max_error under 0.06 on the oval and s-bend, and the first completions on the oval. The likely finish time is about 3 s or a little more. Hypotheses to test next: (a) the wider sensor spread removes most line-loss events; (b) at base_speed 1.4 the robot can finish within 3 s; (c) if max_error still exceeds 0.06 on the slalom, kp is too low for the sharper bends and should rise to about 5. Measurements wanted: completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events and steering_oscillation, per track and per seed.
